You are a programming expert. 
You will be provided with a patch used to fix a bug. 

Your task is summarize the modifications made in the patch.
Your summary should consist of two parts, modifications in each file and their relationships.

The patch modifies a single file: `drivers/net/ethernet/broadcom/genet/bcmgenet.c`.

### Modifications in this file:
- **In function `bcmgenet_put_txcb`**: The order of operations was corrected.
  - *Before*: The `tx_cb_ptr` was calculated based on the current value of `ring->write_ptr`, then the write pointer was rewound (decremented or reset to `end_ptr`).
  - *After*: The write pointer is rewound first, and then `tx_cb_ptr` is computed using the updated (decremented) write pointer.

### Relationship:
The bug was an off-by-one error: the function is supposed to return the `tx_cb` that becomes available after rewinding the write pointer for cleanup. By computing the pointer before the rewind, the function returned the `tx_cb` at the *next* index (the one after the slot being freed), instead of the slot that was just freed. Swapping the operations ensures that the returned `tx_cb` corresponds to the correct descriptor that is being released. This fix ensures proper cleanup of transmitted buffers.

Here is the commit message:
net: bcmgenet: fix off-by-one in bcmgenet_put_txcb

The write_ptr points to the next open tx_cb. We want to return the
tx_cb that gets rewinded, so we must rewind the pointer first then
return the tx_cb that it points to. That way the txcb can be correctly
cleaned up.

Fixes: 876dbadd53a7 ("net: bcmgenet: Fix unmapping of fragments in bcmgenet_xmit()")
Signed-off-by: Justin Chen <justin.chen@broadcom.com>
Reviewed-by: Nicolai Buchwitz <nb@tipi-net.de>
Link: https://patch.msgid.link/20260406175756.134567-2-justin.chen@broadcom.com
Signed-off-by: Jakub Kicinski <kuba@kernel.org>

Here is the root cause:
The function `bcmgenet_put_txcb` incorrectly computed the pointer to the tx_cb before rewinding the write pointer. Since `write_ptr` points to the next available slot, the slot to be released (cleaned up) is the one just before it. By calculating the pointer first using the old `write_ptr` value, the code returned the wrong tx_cb (the next slot), causing an off-by-one error and improper cleanup of transmitted buffers.

Here is the patch:
 
 static struct enet_cb *bcmgenet_put_txcb(struct bcmgenet_priv *priv,
 					 struct bcmgenet_tx_ring *ring)
 {
 	struct enet_cb *tx_cb_ptr;
 
-	tx_cb_ptr = ring->cbs;
-	tx_cb_ptr += ring->write_ptr - ring->cb_ptr;
-
 	/* Rewinding local write pointer */
 	if (ring->write_ptr == ring->cb_ptr)
 		ring->write_ptr = ring->end_ptr;
 	else
 		ring->write_ptr--;
 
+	tx_cb_ptr = ring->cbs;
+	tx_cb_ptr += ring->write_ptr - ring->cb_ptr;
+
 	return tx_cb_ptr;
 }
